published.citation: Shalm et al. (2015) Table I, row '5': N(++|ab) = 6378, N_stop = 12127, total trials 177,358,351, p-value 5.9e-9 and adjusted p-value 2.3e-7 at eps_p = 3e-3. Shalm et al. assumptions.source: Shalm et al. (2015), Supplemental Material Sec. I C and Sec. III D.
assumptions.statement: Both setting predictabilities obey P_A, P_B <= (1 + eps)/2 with eps = 0.003. The largest bias measured on the phase-diffusion generator after synchronisation was (1.08 +/- 0.07)e-4 at Alice and (0.81 +/- 0.02)e-4 at Bob, an excess predictability of about 2e-4; predictability is not measurable by statistical tests, so this bound is an assumption and not a measurement. The authors grant fifteen times the measured bias.

assumptions.source: Shalm et al. (2015), main text; Shalm et al. (2015), Supplemental Material Sec. I C.
assumptions.statement: The two random number generators are physically independent of each other and of the photon properties, beyond the excess predictability granted below. This cannot be established by statistical tests and is the assumption that no Bell test can remove.
Trials are delimited by a 99.1 kHz synchronisation signal available locally at each station, so defining a trial needs no information from the other station.

Undetected trials are counted, not discarded, so the inequality needs no assumption that detected pairs are a fair sample. System detection efficiencies of 74.7 +/- 0.3 % at Alice and 75.6 +/- 0.3 % at Bob clear the 72.5 % threshold that the measured background rates impose.

assumptions.source: Shalm et al. (2015), main text, closing paragraph.
assumptions.statement: A measurement outcome is fixed when the time tagger records it, which happens before information about the other party's setting could arrive.

assumptions.source: Shalm et al. (2015), Supplemental Material Sec. I B.
assumptions.statement: N was fixed before the analysis at 0.9 r f, with f the relevant-trial fraction estimated on a training set and r the trials left after it; later trials were discarded. The p-value bound is invalid at a data-dependent stopping point.

assumptions.source: Shalm et al. (2015), main text Figs. 3 and 4 and Table I.
assumptions.statement: Every setting choice is complete outside the light cone of the photon-pair creation, and each measurement is complete before the other party's setting could be known. For five aggregate pulses the tolerated timing error is 38.3 +/- 3.7 ns and each party is at least 5.4 m inside its locality boundary.

test.inequality: P(++|ab) - P(+0|ab') - P(0+|a'b) - P(++|a'b') <= 0 under local realism. Shalm et al. (2015), Supplemental Material Eq. (S1): the Clauser-Horne form (Phys. Rev. D 10, 526) as used by Eberhard (Phys. Rev. A 47, R747), with the modification of Giustina et al., Nature 497, 227.
test.name: martingale-binomial-ch-eberhard
test.p_value: p <= P(Binomial(N, p0) >= N_S), recomputed here as an exact binomial tail. Shalm et al. (2015), Supplemental Material Eq. (S2), proved in Bierhorst, J. Phys. A 48, 195302 (2015): the indicator sequence of ++ab trials is a supermartingale under local realism, so the bound holds for hidden variables with memory and needs no independent-and-identically-distributed assumption.
test.statistic: T is the sequence of trials whose settings and outcomes lie in {++ab, +0ab', 0+a'b, ++a'b'}; the statistic N_S counts the ++ab trials among the first N elements of T. Shalm et al. (2015), Supplemental Material Sec. I A, with N fixed before the analysis per Sec. I B.
test.success_probability: p0 = 1/2 + eps/(1 + eps^2), the maximum of p_a p_b / (p_a p_b + p_a' p_b') over settings probabilities bounded by (1 + eps)/2, attained at p_a = p_b = (1 + eps)/2. Shalm et al. (2015), Supplemental Material Eq. (S3) and (S4), following Bierhorst, arXiv:1312.2999. At eps = 0 this is 1/2, the equiprobable-settings case.
